cohort: The study included 51 women with pregnancy-triggered atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (p-aHUS) and 397 women of childbearing age with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) and no identified trigger from the Global aHUS Registry.
finding: Eculizumab treatment significantly improved renal outcomes, specifically time to end-stage renal disease (ESRD), in women with aHUS, irrespective of whether their condition was triggered by pregnancy or not.
